newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses climb into record books.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses climb into record books.

text.p: British shares soared through 4,000 points on the key FTSE index for the first time on Wednesday as European share markets bubbled to record highs and the dollar rallied to levels unseen in more than 2-1/2 years.
Frankfurt and Amsterdam also hit records in early trade after the Dow industrials ended above the 5,900 level for the first time as the bond market rallied on surprisingly weak U.S. economic data.
London's blue chip FTSE 100 index shot through 4,000 points at the opening, having fallen just short of the key level on Tuesday, then powered to a high of 4,014.4 in early trade.

"In the very short term, it does appear there's quite a lot of cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to come in and that's going to happen sooner rather than later," said Panmure Gordon strategist Ian Williams.
Dutch shares climbed after news that telecoms group Dutch PTT (KPN) is bidding 2.7 billion guilders ($1.6 billion) for Australia's TNT transport group.
The dollar's overnight strength and Wall Street's own brush with the record books gave European share and debt markets a decisive shove at the start of business.
Europe's other major equity market, Paris, also opened strongly higher, while U.S. buoyancy helped Hong Kong to its best finish this year and the Australian stock market ended at a five-month high.
The dollar steadied in early European business after an Asian sprint to 111.90 yen, its highest level in more than 2-1/2 years against the generally depressed Japanese currency.
Traders said the dollar should have a clear run higher once it managed to hurdle the key 112 yen level.

"We might struggle to get through 112, but if we were to get through, there's an awful lot of people who aren't long of dollars yet. We could have some quite significant technical buying," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston in London.
The onslaught against the yen followed Japan's poor trade position and expectations that capital would continue to flow out of Tokyo, economists said.
By 0900 GMT the dollar was quoted around 111.70 yen and 1.5242 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
Overnight comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in Europe.

London's share traders said an influx of cash at the start of the new quarter, combined with moderate growth and benign inflationary pressures in Britain and the United States provided the backdrop for the stock market's heady rise in recent days.

"On a week to two week view there's probably more upside to come... over the fourth quarter as a whole we're still a little bit nervous... but the underlying liquidity driver is going to be the factor in the near future," said Panmure Gordon's Williams.
The firmer dollar and Wall Street's gains were cited by German traders as the main factors behind the rise of the 30-share DAX index to a record 2,673.27 in early business.
Some were worried, however, that the market could suffer from profit-taking before Thursday's national holiday.
French shares also started well bid on the back of Wall Street's performance and a firm bond market with the CAC-40 nearly 14 points higher at 2,137.19.
"The market is feeling bullish," said one trader. "New York, London are at historic highs, the franc's doing well, the dollar's looking good."
But another trader said the market was looking toppy and said the release on Friday of U.S. jobs figures argued in favour of caution.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.70 yen and 1.5242 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was up 18.5 points at 4,010.7.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index of German shares was up 14.09 at 2,669.82.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 13.98 at 2,137.19.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened firmer at $379.40 an ounce versus Tuesday's London close of $378.65 as short covering underpinned the market. Silver was steady at $4.91. ($1=1.708 Guilder)
